feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for senior digital communications roles: the progression at NACo is clear, the scope is substantial, and the profile aligns well with the target title. Writing is polished overall, but the document is somewhat repetitive, light on measurable outcomes beyond web scale, and has a few style/grammar inconsistencies.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear career progression within one organization, showing increasing responsibility from coordinator to director to consultant.  
- Strong domain fit: digital strategy, CMS modernization, analytics, multimedia, and advocacy/public-sector communications are all well evidenced.  
- Good credibility signals through concrete platform detail and scale indicators (10,000+ pages, 3.5 million annual page views, 50+ publishers).

1. Top improvements  
- Add more impact metrics: include results for email, social, video, campaign performance, team size, budget, efficiency gains, or stakeholder outcomes to strengthen achievement focus.  
- Reduce duplication across “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT”; consolidate to improve structure and save space.  
- Fix minor writing/style issues: “12 years experience” should be “12 years’ experience” or “more than 12 years of experience”; use serial commas consistently (“content operations, and enterprise web improvement” vs other lists); standardize hyphenation/style across terms like “organization-wide/organisation-wide,” “front-end,” and date abbreviations (“Sept.”/“Mar.”/“Oct.”).
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary that aligns well with the CV’s direction, but it reads slightly generic and repeats language already covered in Core Competencies and Topline Skills. Tightening it and adding a clearer leadership/value angle would improve impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Change “more than 12 years experience” to “12+ years of experience” for cleaner, standard phrasing.
- Lead with current senior positioning and outcomes focus, e.g. digital strategy, platform modernization, and communications operations for mission-driven/public-sector organizations.
- Reduce the long channel list (“web, content, email, social media, and multimedia”) to avoid sounding inventory-like; emphasize cross-channel leadership instead.
- Suggested rewrite: Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years of experience leading cross-channel content, web, email, social, and multimedia programs for mission-driven organizations. Brings deep expertise in digital strategy, platform modernization, and building the workflows, governance, and systems that enable effective communications at scale. Strong in advocacy messaging, stakeholder coordination, and translating technical or policy issues into clear, accessible content.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-channel communications,” “platform modernization,” and workflow/systems language overlap heavily with Core Competencies and Topline Skills.
- “Advocacy messaging” is reinforced throughout NACo roles, so keep it concise here.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block is broad and overlaps heavily with the summary, Topline Skills, and Soft Skills. Tightening the phrasing and emphasizing higher-value leadership/strategy capabilities will make it more distinctive.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace generic terms with sharper, CV-aligned phrasing: “Multi-channel communications leadership,” “CMS modernization & administration,” “Editorial systems & governance,” “Analytics, insights & performance reporting.”
- Reorder for relevance/seniority: lead with strategy, digital operations, platforms, analytics, and governance; place multimedia/event production last.
- Use parallel noun phrases and consistent style throughout; change “communication” to “communications” for consistency.
- Suggested rewrite: Digital strategy & transformation • Multi-channel communications leadership • CMS administration & web operations • Editorial systems & workflow design • Analytics, insights & performance reporting • Workflow architecture & process improvement • Cross-functional stakeholder coordination • Policy & advocacy communications • Multimedia & live event production

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination” duplicates Soft Skills and the header.
- Several items overlap with Topline Skills; consider shortening this section or using it only for broad themes.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Consult a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant current role, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with the NACo director role and Recent Projects. Make it sharper, more consultative, and focused on current high-value contributions.

Suggested edit
- Open with scope + seniority: “Advise NACo on enterprise digital strategy, web governance, campaign architecture, and communications operations as an external consultant.”
- Consolidate execution bullets into 3–4 impact-led bullets, e.g.:
- “Designed and implemented Drupal-based campaign experiences, including modular microsites, storytelling components, and downloadable member toolkits.”
- “Improved cross-channel communications operations by refining workflows, analytics, and governance across web, email, social, and multimedia.”
- “Led an AI-enabled search initiative, defining retrieval strategy, structured content requirements, and user-facing discovery experience.”
- Replace generic phrases like “deliver technical troubleshooting” with stronger outcomes: “resolved platform issues,” “improved publishing efficiency,” or “supported scalable site operations.”
- Add metrics if possible: number of sites/campaigns launched, workflow time reduced, engagement lift, search success improvements.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Build/refine digital systems, workflows and analytics” overlaps with the 2022–2024 director role.
- Microsite and AI search bullets duplicate Recent Projects; keep this entry higher-level and save specifics for projects.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It should be tightened to foreground the biggest outcomes and distinguish strategic leadership from the more execution-focused NACo roles before and after it.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper summary: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Combine channel oversight bullets and add outcomes where possible: email open/click growth, social engagement growth, production volume, or cost/time savings from the in-house studio.
- Rewrite the website bullet to emphasize transformation and complexity: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Tighten governance/analytics bullets into impact language: “Built enterprise reporting across GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery, enabling faster leadership reporting and stronger cross-department planning.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Video as a recurring channel” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; keep this entry focused on building the studio and scaling capacity.
- Governance/workflow language overlaps with the current consultant role; emphasize ownership and enterprise scope here.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the roles before and after it. Make it more specific to what changed under your ownership at this level, with tighter phrasing and clearer outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope + function: “Managed day-to-day digital communications across NACo’s web, email, social and video channels, improving coordination for advocacy and member communications.”
- Tighten bullets to distinct contributions: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Reframe video bullet around growth/launch impact: “Produced and scaled a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Combine workflow/editorial bullets: “Built stronger editorial planning and cross-team coordination across communications, advocacy and program staff, improving publishing consistency and execution.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital communications across web, email, social and video” is repeated in the Director of Digital Media role; keep this version more execution-focused, not leadership/governance-focused.
- Weekly video updates also appear in the 2015–2018 role; emphasize scaling/formalizing the series here rather than originating it.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this item is too generic and overlaps heavily with the header, Core Competencies, and recent NACo roles. Tighten it to emphasize higher-value leadership capabilities not already repeated elsewhere.

Suggested edit:
- Replace broad phrases with sharper, senior-level wording tied to recent scope:
- Enterprise digital strategy & governance
- Editorial operations for high-volume publishing
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector advocacy and stakeholder messaging
- Audience-centered content strategy
- Consider swapping “Audience-focused content planning” for “Content operations and governance” or “Executive-level digital communications strategy” to better reflect director/consultant-level work.
- Keep terminology consistent with the rest of the CV: use either “multi-channel” or “cross-channel” throughout.
- If space allows, add one scale cue in the heading or nearby summary instead of here (e.g., “10,000+ page platforms” or “50+ publishers”).

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “Editorial systems and governance” duplicate Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” is already covered in Core Competencies and multiple NACo roles.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it reads as a generic tool list and overlaps heavily with the Technical + IT section. This topline item should be tighter, more strategic, and emphasize the platforms/technical strengths most supported by recent roles.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from a long list to a sharper capability summary: “Drupal and enterprise CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based content systems • AI-enabled search experiences”
- Put Drupal first and consider dropping WordPress/SharePoint/Power Pages here unless they are important for target roles; they are already covered in Technical + IT.
- Replace “Airtable systems” with “Airtable-based content systems” or “Airtable workflow systems” for clearer business value.
- If space allows, make one item outcome-oriented: “CMS modernization for high-volume public-sector sites” to echo the 10,000+ page migration.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item duplicates much of “Technical + IT”; keep topline skills strategic, not exhaustive.
- “AI-enabled search experiences” also appears in Core Competencies, so avoid repeating it elsewhere verbatim.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tools list, but it reads as a generic inventory and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” analytics section. This topline item should emphasize strategic analytics capability over repeating platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tool list to outcome-oriented capability cluster, e.g.: “Analytics strategy, KPI design, executive reporting, SEO/performance analysis”
- Keep only the most differentiating tools here and group them: “GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity”
- Tighten phrasing for consistency: use parallel nouns, not mixed tools + activities
- Suggested rewrite: “Analytics strategy & optimization: KPI design, executive reporting, SEO/performance analysis, and dashboarding across GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, and Microsoft Clarity”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Current wording duplicates “Analytics and reporting infrastructure” in Core Competencies and “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT
- Avoid adding “A/B testing” unless you can support it in recent experience; prioritize analytics infrastructure and reporting, which are better evidenced in the 2022–present roles

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill area, but it reads generic and overlaps with both Core Competencies and Technical + IT. Tighten it to emphasize operational scope and higher-value delivery rather than listing basic production tasks.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe toward leadership and delivery: “Broadcast-quality video production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • PTZ camera and studio systems • Virtual event operations”
- Consider replacing “Video production and editing” with “Broadcast-quality video production” to better match the in-house studio achievement in the 2022–2024 role.
- Use parallel phrasing and remove filler: keep all items as noun phrases, 4 bullets max.
- If you can support it elsewhere, add scale in adjacent experience bullets rather than here (e.g., recurring programs, in-house studio build, event support volume).

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Livestreaming” overlaps with “Multimedia production and livestream operations” in Core Competencies.
- Tool-level detail here partly duplicates “Livestream studio workflows” under Technical + IT; keep this section focused on capability, not software/tools.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant platform list, but it’s too bare and overlaps with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. This item should either add specificity or be tightened to avoid repeating the same keywords elsewhere.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe to show level/relevance, e.g. “Drupal (enterprise/public-sector), WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages, GitHub Pages.”
- Put the strongest, most recent platform first and consider dropping the weakest/least strategic item if space is tight: “Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages.”
- If accurate, add version/scope detail for impact: “Drupal 10” or “enterprise CMS platforms” to align with the 10,000+ page migration in recent roles.
- Consider renaming the heading to “CMS & Web Platforms” for cleaner phrasing.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates Topline Skills [2], which already lists Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages plus broader web execution skills.
- “GitHub Pages” may feel minor relative to the seniority and impact of recent enterprise platform work.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” For a senior digital leader, this item should emphasize implementation scope and modern tools rather than basic languages alone.

Suggested edit:
- Retitle to something more outcome-oriented, e.g. “Front-End Development & Technical Implementation.”
- Tighten and modernize phrasing: “HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery, API integrations, Google Tag Manager, Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions.”
- If accurate, add level/scope instead of just tools: “Front-end implementation for Drupal-based public websites; API-driven integrations; deployment/workflow automation via GitHub Actions; edge scripting with Cloudflare Workers.”
- Consider dropping version numbers (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) unless used consistently elsewhere; “HTML, CSS, JavaScript” is cleaner and more current.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This substantially duplicates Topline Skills [2] (“HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery,” “API integrations”).
- GTM may fit better under “Data, Analytics & Optimization” unless you want this section strictly implementation-focused.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item mixes true automation platforms with general collaboration/project tools, which weakens the “systems” signal. It also overlaps with “Workflow automation and platform integration” in Core Competencies and “Airtable systems / Workflow automation” in Topline Skills.

Suggested edit:
- Split by function or tighten the label to emphasize automation-first tools.
- Rewrite as: **Automation & Workflow Tools:** Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira Automations
- Move general collaboration tools to a separate line if space allows: **Project & Collaboration:** Asana • Basecamp • Trello • Slack • Microsoft Teams
- If these tools were used at meaningful scale, add that in experience bullets instead of here (e.g., “built cross-team Airtable/Power Automate workflows used by 50+ publishers”).

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Slack” and “Teams” read as generic workplace tools unless tied to workflow orchestration.
- “Airtable systems” and “Workflow automation” already appear elsewhere; avoid repeating the same value proposition without outcomes.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is relevant, but it reads as a bare vendor list and misses the operational/email leadership context shown in recent NACo roles. It should signal platform administration or campaign execution without repeating broader “multi-channel communications” claims already covered elsewhere.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms**
- Tighten platform names for readability: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp**
- If accurate, add a light qualifier to show applied use, e.g. **newsletter operations, audience segmentation, campaign journeys**
- Consider ordering by strongest/recentest relevance: put the platform most used at NACo first

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps with work experience bullets about leading email newsletters; keep this item tool-focused, not responsibility-focused
- Avoid repeating “communications,” “campaigns,” or “audience reach” language already established in recent roles

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is still broad and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more foundational and execution-focused, with concrete scope or outputs if you can quantify them.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to emphasize early-team building and hands-on delivery: “Promoted through two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team, supporting web, email, social and multimedia operations.”
- Add measurable outcomes where possible: website refresh scope, number/frequency of livestreams or weekly videos, audience reach, or growth in output/engagement.
- Tighten the closing clause to show supervision more clearly: “Mentored a digital media associate on daily production and publishing workflows.”
- Possible version: “Promoted through two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team, improving workflows across web, email, social and multimedia. Supported a major website refresh and produced recurring digital content, including livestreams and weekly video updates, while mentoring a digital media associate on day-to-day production.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 advocacy video bullet; differentiate this as the earlier launch/build phase.
- “strengthening workflows” repeats language used in later NACo entries; keep this version more tactical.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry with a credible “first podcast” achievement, but it reads broadly and overlaps with later NACo digital/media roles. Emphasize the podcast launch and any concrete project outputs, while keeping the rest concise.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to foreground the standout outcome: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting county policy and program teams; launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, scripting, guest coordination and production.”
- Trim generic phrasing like “contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials”; replace with a specific deliverable if possible (e.g., articles, videos, toolkits, research briefs).
- Add measurable scope where available: number of projects supported, episodes produced, stakeholders served, or audiences reached.
- If space allows, split into 2 bullets: one for research/program support, one for podcast launch and multimedia execution.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid overemphasizing general digital content/multimedia work, which is covered more strongly in later NACo roles.
- “First podcast” is distinctive; keep that, but don’t repeat broad video/media language already used in 2015–2024 entries.
